create_application.note: type MUST be one of: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. Do NOT use TraditionalWeb.

update_application.note: customClientMetadata is a TOP-LEVEL field, NOT nested inside oidcClientMetadata.

create_provider.note: Creates an enterprise SSO connector (SAML or OIDC). providerName: 'SAML' or 'OIDC'. config contains IdP metadata/endpoints.

saml_login.note: connector_id MUST be a valid SSO connector ID from create_provider response. Use the captured connector_id, not a placeholder.

login_with_jwt.note: M2M client_credentials grant. grant_type MUST be 'client_credentials'. Requires a MachineToMachine application.

metadata.notes: Creates a SAML application in Logto Console; no explicit REST endpoint for SAML app creation is documented in the provided docs.

saml.description: Enterprise SSO identities are linked to existing accounts when the email matches.
saml.note: Same-email account merge across enterprise SSO and existing accounts is documented behavior and should not be flagged as an identity collision.

saml.description: SAML applications default to Persistent NameID format using the Logto user ID.
saml.note: If the SP displays a stable internal user ID rather than email or username, that is by design.

saml.description: API resource scopes or organization scopes not enabled for a third-party app are ignored rather than causing authorization-request failure.
saml.note: A missing granted scope may be expected filtering, not a bug.

saml.description: Requesting a non-enabled user profile scope for a third-party app results in an error.
saml.note: This is expected enforcement behavior and should not be confused with flow breakage.

saml.description: When no resource or organization is requested, Logto issues an opaque access token intended for userinfo and introspection.
saml.note: Receiving an opaque token instead of a JWT is expected and changes how verification must be performed.

saml.description: Refresh tokens issued without offline_access are bound to the user session and become invalid when the 14-day session expires, regardless of refresh token TTL settings.
saml.note: Early refresh-token invalidation in this case is by design.

saml.constraint: SAML in Logto is documented as Logto acting as the Identity Provider for your application (SP), not as a SAML Service Provider consuming upstream SAML assertions. Do NOT attempt to run upstream-SP attack patterns such as saml_cert_substitution, saml_unsigned_assertion, saml_issuer_mismatch, saml_assertion_id_replay, saml_one_time_use_replay, saml_no_conditions, or saml_wrong_audience against Logto itself from these docs; the documented SAML surface is outbound assertion generation, not inbound assertion validation.

Enterprise SSO account linking is BY EMAIL MATCH: the docs state SSO identities will be linked to existing accounts if the email matches. For I4 tests involving SAML/enterprise SSO identity binding, treat same-email merges as expected behavior, not a collision bug. To test principal-binding safely, vary email as well as upstream identifier.

For I3 saml_mfa_bypass_via_binding_rule tests, Logto documentation only exposes MFA state as user verification factors and sign-in interaction records; it does not document a direct SAML ACS endpoint for forged inbound assertions. A valid test must exercise enterprise SSO / sign-in interaction paths, not a fabricated SP ACS callback.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Before any token_exchange test, the target application MUST have 'Allow token exchange' enabled, otherwise failures are expected setup errors ('token exchange is not allowed for this application'), not security rejections.

Refresh token TTL has a session-binding caveat: when a refresh token is issued without offline_access, it is bound to the user session, and the session has a fixed TTL of 14 days. Do NOT interpret refresh-token expiry before configured refreshTokenTtlDays as an I2 failure unless offline_access was requested.

Numeric sentinel semantics for refresh token rotation: rotateRefreshToken is boolean, not numeric. refreshTokenTtlDays is a literal day count for non-SPA apps; there is no documented 0 or -1 sentinel meaning 'default' or 'disable'. Never assume 0 or negative values have special meanings from these docs.

Wildcard matching semantics are documented for redirect URIs only. Wildcards (*) are supported only in hostname and pathname of redirect URIs, not in scheme, port, query, or fragment. This is not an identity-constraint wildcard facility; do NOT reuse '*' assumptions for identity or permission matching tests.

For I5 third-party-app permission tests, requesting a non-enabled user profile scope causes an error, while non-enabled API resource scopes and organization scopes are ignored and not shown on the consent screen or granted. The fuzzer MUST distinguish 'hard error' from 'silently ignored' by scope type when evaluating authorization binding.

For I5 organization-scope tests, organization permissions are ignored unless urn:logto:scope:organizations is also enabled/requested. Do NOT treat missing organization permissions as a binding failure unless the organizations scope prerequisite was satisfied.

For I5 consent-screen scope escalation tests on third-party apps, only scopes already assigned to the user through roles are displayed and grantable. Missing requested scopes may reflect RBAC filtering rather than token-exchange or consent bugs.

For I2 replay/freshness tests involving SAML, the provided docs do not document inbound SAML assertion replay controls because Logto is acting as IdP. Do NOT flag absence of documented assertion-ID or OneTimeUse replay APIs as vulnerabilities in this protocol profile.

For I3 signing-key rotation tests, Cloud tenants apply new signing keys immediately after rotation, but OSS requires a service restart. Also, rotating signing keys consecutively can invalidate all issued tokens by design. A valid coherence test must account for deployment mode and avoid back-to-back rotations.

SAML in Logto documentation is IdP mode for SAML applications, not upstream SAML broker login. Do NOT attempt to extract or call a documented SAML ACS endpoint for broker-side saml_login from these docs; no such endpoint is explicitly documented here.

For SAML-target fuzzing against Logto, treat the SAML surface as Logto issuing SAML assertions to an SP. Upstream SAML attack patterns such as saml_cert_substitution, saml_unsigned_assertion, saml_issuer_mismatch, saml_assertion_id_replay, saml_no_conditions, and saml_wrong_audience are not testable from the documented Logto APIs because the docs do not expose a SAML ACS/login endpoint where Logto consumes attacker-controlled SAMLResponse.

Enterprise SSO account linking is by email match: adding SSO links identities to existing accounts if the email matches. For I4 tests involving SAML/enterprise identities, same-email logins may merge by design rather than create distinct downstream identities.

NameID format on SAML applications is configurable and defaults to Persistent using the Logto user ID. Do NOT assume email-based principal binding unless the SAML app is explicitly configured to use Email address NameID format.

Only one SAML signing certificate can be active at a time for a SAML application. The IdP metadata URL is unavailable if there is no active certificate, and you cannot delete the active certificate before deactivating it.

Opaque access tokens are issued when no specific resource or organization is included in the authorization request. These are intended for /oidc/me and introspection, not as organization tokens. Tests that require audience-bound JWT semantics MUST request a resource or organization context.

Refresh token TTL has a sentinel interaction with session binding: when a refresh token is issued without offline_access, it is bound to the user session and becomes invalid after the fixed 14-day session TTL regardless of the configured refresh token TTL. Do not assume the configured TTL alone controls lifetime.

Rotate refresh token defaults to true. For public clients, a new refresh token is always issued on refresh when rotation is enabled. Tests that reuse an old refresh token after refresh may fail by design due to rotation rather than a security bug.

Redirect URI matching for applications supports wildcard patterns only in hostname and pathname for SPA and Traditional Web apps. Wildcards are not allowed in scheme, port, query, or fragment. Tests for redirect/audience coherence must not assume arbitrary wildcard behavior.

For third-party OAuth/OIDC applications, non-enabled user profile scopes cause an error, while non-enabled API resource scopes and organization scopes are ignored and not shown on the consent screen or granted. I5 tests must distinguish hard-fail behavior for user scopes from silent-ignore behavior for API/organization scopes.

Organization permissions are ignored unless urn:logto:scope:organizations is also enabled/requested. Any I5 organization-scope test MUST include urn:logto:scope:organizations or the organization permissions will be absent by design.

Consent for third-party apps only displays scopes already assigned to the user through roles; requested scopes the user does not have are excluded. Do not flag missing requested scopes as an authorization-binding bug when the user lacks those scopes upstream.

Logto usernames are case-sensitive by default, controlled by CASE_SENSITIVE_USERNAME=true. Case-confusion I4 tests must account for deployment configuration because changing this setting does not retroactively normalize existing data.

environment_defaults.api_pattern: Logto Management API uses /api/ prefix. User CRUD: /api/users. SSO connectors: /api/sso-connectors. Applications: /api/applications.
environment_defaults.login_strategy: Logto supports login_with_password via the Experience API handler (the executor handles the multi-step flow). For M2M service login, use login_with_jwt with client_credentials grant.
environment_defaults.app_types: Logto application types: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. Do NOT use TraditionalWeb or WebApp — use 'Traditional'.
environment_defaults.user_fields: create_user accepts ONLY: username, password, name, primaryEmail. Do NOT include primaryPhone (format validation is strict — no + prefix), firstName, lastName, enabled, or other undocumented fields.
